subject.title: iOS remote pairing UX: QR crash, onboarding paste fails, Settings paste works (cellular); feedback on edge auth + mobile wss://

question: Should OpenClaw document an advanced public mobile `wss://` pairing recipe with split admin and mobile hostnames, and exactly what auth boundary should it recommend relative to Tailscale Serve and trusted-proxy auth?
rationale: The code path can support secure public `wss://` setup codes, but the requested recipe tells operators where to place or bypass edge identity gates, which is a product and security-boundary decision automation should not settle.

options.title: Document advanced split-host recipe
options.body: Add a security-reviewed docs section that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while covering a dedicated mobile `wss://` hostname, OpenClaw bootstrap/device auth, `trustedProxies`, `allowedOrigins`, and explicit warnings about browser SSO redirects on the mobile path.

options.title: Defer public `wss://` guidance
options.body: Keep docs limited to Tailscale Serve and generic exposure guidance until maintainers are ready to support public mobile pairing as a documented deployment pattern.

options.title: Require product design first
options.body: Open a narrower design issue for first-class edge access policy support before documenting manual split-host workarounds.

recommendation.title: Document advanced split-host recipe
recommendation.body: Add a security-reviewed docs section that keeps Tailscale Serve as the default while covering a dedicated mobile `wss://` hostname, OpenClaw bootstrap/device auth, `trustedProxies`, `allowedOrigins`, and explicit warnings about browser SSO redirects on the mobile path.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current Tailnet pairing fix and appear as the strongest current owner across the device-pair, iOS gateway, and exposure-docs surfaces.
